newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker in sporadic trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker in sporadic trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed weaker at C$1.3680 (US$0.7310) on Thursday from Wednesday's close at C$1.3665 (US$0.7318) in sporadic trading, dealers said. * They said the weakness stemmed from yesterday's comments from the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman and rumors leading up to news that a large Canadian department store chain was in trouble.
"It wasn't as bad as everyone had been thinking," said one trader.

The currency also softened in the aftermath of comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. He said on Wednesday that a pre-emptive interest rate hike aimed at controlling inflation could not be ruled out.
A few orders from large funds to sell the Canadian dollar also softened the currency, dealers said.
"There was heavy interest to sell Canada," said one trader.
The market will be watching closely for numbers tomorrow.

Statistics Canada plans to release numbers for the fourth- quarter 1996 current account balance and gross domestic product. A Reuters survey of economists forecast a fall of C$3 billion in the fourth-quarter current account balance.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slipped to 1.2340 marks from 1.2358 on Wednesday and to 88.18 yen from Wednesday's 89.18 yen.
